title: Trips to New York, crowd reaction and band dissension
summary: Blumberg gives how often he visited, how the crowd stood before the bandstand, the factional arguments over Bunk and Jim Robinson, and that Gene ran the engagement.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Oh, I see. How often would you get up to New York in that period when you first went up there?

I don't remember. I think it was about, maybe two times during the first engagement, and maybe two times, the whole thing was probably, uh, well, it must have been more than that. I, I guess it was around seven or eight times, all together with the two engagements.
For a few days each time, you know.
You moved up there later on. Later on, yeah.
What about the reaction of the crowd up there, to the music, uh, other than the dancing? What did they do?

Well, there would be a, uh, a large group usually standing right in front of the bandstand, which was, uh, pretty high up off the floor. I think the bandstand was about, uh, four, three or four feet up, off the floor. And, uh, maybe even more than that. Well, about four feet. And, uh, we'd all be standing there. I would be one of the, one of the crowd standing in front of the bandstand, and looking up at various, uh, idols, you know. And, uh, during a good deal of this time, there was, uh, dissension in the band. And, uh, actually it was kind of comical that there would be a group standing in front of Jim Robinson, who would be listening to him play his solo parts and so forth. And, uh, I remember there was a woman there who would turn around and sneer at Bunk, you know. Every time Jim played something real good. And I guess there were others that did the same thing back, although I don't remember that. But, uh, there were some, uh, animated, uh, uh, discussions on the part of the factions as well as on the part of the musicians. I remember going to a party down in the village during that time and, uh, got into a big argument down there over, uh, who was right in the band, you know. So, uh, it was quite lively.
What would they do at the end of the number? People, what would their reaction be?
Oh, usually applaud, I, I, yeah, I suppose.
They wouldn't scream and holler like they do to Indian Whistle and all that carry-on.
People don't do that in New York.
No, this was, well, they probably do, but not these people. Yeah. This is a more, uh, wholesome group.
Well, who seemed to be running the thing, just from the standpoint of an outsider?

Well, I guess Gene was running it. Uh, uh, he had some kind of, uh, tie-in with the owner of the Stuyvesant, Mr. Menschel or something like that. And, uh, as far as I know, it was Gene that, uh, that engineered the thing. And, uh, later on, I think he went out and, and, uh, uh, did something similar with Kid Orrie's band, I believe. I know he was quite active.
